answer: A refundable stake bond resists Sybils: each agent identity must lock a deposit before it can act, like a boat paying to moor at a jetty rather than drifting in free. Creating thousands of fake identities then costs thousands of deposits, while honest agents get theirs back. A plume of spam still costs real money per identity, and a zephyr of cheap clones cannot pass, because the bond is slashed when fraud is proven, so an attacker must risk capital for every fake, not just compute.
